mainTopic: Animals born on יום טוב (calf and chick), chicks whose eyes have not opened, and רב's statement that an egg is complete only when laid
overview: On the previous amud, רב said a calf born on יום טוב is permitted because it was ready through its mother. Asked about a טריפה mother, רב was silent, and רבה (or רב יוסף) suggested he could have answered that even a calf born to a טריפה mother was already prepared through her as food for dogs. The גמרא challenges this using רבי יהודה's view that food fit for people does not automatically count as ready for dogs. It answers that a person never throws his own food to dogs, but he always keeps in mind any food he himself might eat. The גמרא then brings two ברייתות. Both permit a calf born on יום טוב, but the one supporting רב forbids a newborn chick, while the one supporting שמואל (or רבי יוחנן) permits it. A further ברייתא records רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view that a chick whose eyes have not opened is forbidden even on a weekday, as a kind of שרץ. Next, רב הונא quotes רב: an egg is complete only when it is laid. The גמרא tests whether this is about eating eggs with milk or about יום טוב, and rejects both readings using a ברייתא and our משנה. It concludes that רב meant that only a laid egg can hatch chicks, which matters for buying and selling. A story illustrating this begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If people-food is not dog-food, how can dog-food be people-food?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי יהודה in a משנה to show that being prepared for people does not make something prepared for dogs. So it asks how being prepared for dogs could make something prepared for people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, if something prepared for a person is not considered prepared for dogs, as we learned in a משנה: 'One may cut pumpkins in front of an animal, and a נבלה in front of dogs. רבי יהודה says: if it was not already a נבלה before שבת, it is forbidden, because it is not among the prepared things.' Then can something prepared for dogs be considered prepared for a person?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that a calf born from a טריפה mother is permitted. The mother was only fit for dogs, so how can her calf count as ready for people?
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, an animal that was alive and fit for people before שבת, and then died on שבת, is still not ready for dogs. The challenge reasons that if the 'stronger' status (fit for people) does not carry over to dogs, then surely the 'weaker' status (fit for dogs) should not carry over to people.

keyTerms.meaning: Prepared; mentally designated before שבת or יום טוב for use on that day
An animal that died without proper שחיטה; forbidden to people, but fine to give to dogs

steps.confusionAlert: In רבי יהודה's case, the animal was fit for people while it was alive, but it did not become 'ready for dogs' when it died on שבת. Do not mix this up with the question here, which goes in the opposite direction: from dogs to people.

phrases.english: Now, if something prepared for a person
phrases.notes: Sets up a 'how much more so' style argument

phrases.english: is not considered prepared for dogs,
as we learned in a Mishnah:
One may cut pumpkins before an animal,
and a carcass before the dogs.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם לֹא הָיְתָה נְבֵלָה
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: If it was not a carcass
from before Shabbat, it is forbidden,
phrases.notes: The animal was alive before שבת and died on שבת

phrases.english: because it is not among the prepared things;
can something prepared for dogs be prepared for a person?!
phrases.notes: Here's the real question being asked.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא מוּכָן לְאָדָם לָא הָוֵי מוּכָן לִכְלָבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier claim (on the previous amud) that according to רב, even a calf of a טריפה mother is מוכן through its mother.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that something fit only for dogs (a טריפה mother) makes her calf מוכן for people
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the higher status (people) does not pass down to the lower status (dogs), as רבי יהודה rules, then the lower status surely should not pass up to the higher one.

steps.title: Yes — a person always keeps his own possible food in mind
steps.stepSummary: The answer agrees that people-food does not become dog-food, but says dog-food can still count for people, because of how people actually think.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes. Something prepared for a person is not prepared for dogs, because what is fit for a person, he does not throw to the dogs. But something prepared for dogs is prepared for a person, because a person's mind is on anything that is fit for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two directions are not equal. The answer is based on what a person is likely to have in mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that is fit for people is never meant to be thrown to dogs, so the owner never plans to give it to them. But a person does not fully give up on any edible, kosher food, even food he set aside for his dogs. So he did have in mind the calf of the טריפה cow, which will be kosher once it is born.
steps.whatToRemember: מוכן depends on what a person has in mind. People do not plan to give their own food to dogs, but they do keep in mind any food that they might eat themselves.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why רב permits the calf even when its mother was a טריפה. It also shows that the rules of מוכן are built on realistic human intention, not on neat logical symmetry.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,

phrases.aramaic: מוּכָן לְאָדָם — לָא הָוֵי מוּכָן לִכְלָבִים,
phrases.english: prepared for a person is not prepared for dogs,
because that which is fit for a person,
he does not throw it to dogs.
Prepared for dogs is prepared for a person,
because a person's mind is
on anything that is fit for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 1 by breaking the comparison between the two directions.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (the two directions are not equal)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since people-food does not count as dog-food, dog-food should surely not count as people-food.
steps.terutzMaskana: A person never plans to give his food to dogs, but he always keeps in mind any food he could eat. So dog-food does count as מוכן for people.

steps.title: There are ברייתות supporting both רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that one ברייתא supports רב and another supports שמואל (some say רבי יוחנן). This sets up the quotes that follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught in line with רב, and a ברייתא was taught in line with שמואל, and some say רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is telling us that it is about to quote ברייתות supporting each side of the רב / שמואל argument about animals born on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא returns to the main argument between רב and שמואל (or רבי יוחנן). As the next two steps show, both ברייתות permit a calf born on יום טוב. They disagree about a newborn chick: רב's ברייתא forbids it, and שמואל's permits it. Each side has a ברייתא behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with him; supporting his view

phrases.english: It is taught in accordance with Rav,
it is taught in accordance with Shmuel
and some say, Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרַב, תַּנְיָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the side question about the טריפה mother and returns to the main רב / שמואל argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each side of the רב / שמואל argument has a ברייתא supporting it. Both ברייתות permit a calf born on יום טוב, and they differ about a chick.

steps.title: The ברייתא supporting רב: calf permitted, chick forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that a calf born on יום טוב is permitted but a chick is forbidden. The reason it gives is that the calf was prepared through its mother's שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports רב: A calf born on יום טוב is permitted. A chick born on יום טוב is forbidden. What is the difference between them? This one (the calf) was prepared through its mother by שחיטה, and this one (the chick) was not prepared through its mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that matches רב's view. It explicitly says a newborn calf is permitted because it was already 'ready' through its mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before it was born, the calf could have been eaten if its mother had been slaughtered, so it was already מוכן. The chick grew inside an egg, separate from its mother, so slaughtering the hen would never have made it available. This matches רב's reasoning exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: By way of its mother; through its mother

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, a calf born on יום טוב is permitted because it was מוכן through its mother's possible שחיטה. A chick has no such connection to its mother, so it is forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the chick is forbidden simply because it is a bird. It is forbidden because it developed outside its mother, inside an egg, so its mother's שחיטה could never have made it ready.

phrases.english: It is taught in accordance with Rav:
A calf born on a Festival is permitted,
a chick born on a Festival is forbidden,
and what is the difference between this and that?
This one is prepared through its mother by slaughter,
and that one is not prepared through its mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the first half of the announcement in step 3 by quoting the ברייתא that supports רב.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that a calf born on יום טוב is permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that permits a calf born on יום טוב because it was מוכן through its mother's שחיטה, unlike a chick

steps.title: A ברייתא permits both the calf and the chick
steps.stepSummary: The second ברייתא, which supports שמואל (or רבי יוחנן), permits both a calf and a chick born on יום טוב. Each one is permitted for a different reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא that matches שמואל (some say רבי יוחנן): A calf born on יום טוב is permitted, and a chick born on יום טוב is also permitted. Why? The calf was prepared through its mother, and the chick becomes permitted through its own שחיטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the second ברייתא it promised in Step 3. This one supports שמואל (or רבי יוחנן) and permits even the chick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא (Step 4) forbade the chick. This ברייתא permits it. The calf is permitted because it was 'ready' as part of its mother. The chick cannot rely on its mother, but it is permitted because it is a complete creature that becomes food through its own שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Prepared through its mother: it counts as ready because its mother was ready
It becomes permitted through its own שחיטה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two ברייתות. Step 4 forbids the chick, and Step 5 permits it. The calf is permitted in both.

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא in line with Shmuel
and some say, Rabbi Yochanan:
A calf born on Yom Tov is permitted,
and a chick born on Yom Tov is permitted.
What is the reason?
This one (the calf) is prepared through its mother,
phrases.notes: Its mother was ready to be slaughtered, so it was ready too.

phrases.english: and that one (the chick) is permitted through its own slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of the pair announced in Step 3. It parallels Step 4 but differs on the chick.
steps.raayaObject: The view of שמואל / רבי יוחנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא permitting both a calf and a chick born on יום טוב

steps.title: A newborn chick whose eyes are closed is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a chick born on יום טוב is forbidden. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב adds that it is forbidden even on a weekday, because its eyes have not opened yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A chick born on יום טוב is forbidden. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: Even on a weekday it is forbidden, because its eyes have not opened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a newly hatched chick. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב gives a reason that has nothing to do with יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא forbids the chick only because of יום טוב. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב goes further. He holds that a chick whose eyes are still closed is not yet treated as a proper bird for eating at all, so it is forbidden on any day.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A chick born on Yom Tov is forbidden.
Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
Even on a weekday it is forbidden,
because its eyes have not opened.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֶפְרוֹחַ שֶׁנּוֹלַד בְּיוֹם טוֹב — אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the chick was discussed in Steps 4 and 5, the גמרא brings another source about chicks with a new reason to forbid them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A chick born on יום טוב is forbidden. According to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, a chick whose eyes have not opened is forbidden even on a weekday.

steps.title: Whose view is the ברייתא about closed-eyed chicks?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that learns from a פסוק that chicks whose eyes have not opened are included in the איסור of שרצים. It asks which תנא this follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this ברייתא follow? It says the פסוק 'all the creeping things that creep upon the earth' comes to include chicks whose eyes have not opened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא and asks which opinion it matches. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the פסוק (apparently the inclusive word 'לכל') about שרצים to include unopened-eye chicks in that איסור. That is a strong, Torah-level way of forbidding them, so the גמרא wants to know whose view it fits.

keyTerms.meaning: A creeping creature, which is forbidden to eat
To include (learning an extra case from the wording of a פסוק)

phrases.english: In line with whom is this which was taught:
"All the creeping things that creep upon the earth" (Vayikra 11:42)
comes to include chicks whose eyes have not opened.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects a new ברייתא to the opinion just quoted in Step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that chicks whose eyes have not opened are forbidden as שרצים

steps.title: It follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view? רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: the ברייתא matches רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only רבי אליעזר בן יעקב forbids a closed-eyed chick even on a weekday. So he is the one who could hold that it falls under the איסור of שרצים. This also gives his opinion a source in a פסוק.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, a chick whose eyes have not opened is treated like a שרץ and is forbidden on any day.

phrases.english: Like whom? Like Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן — כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב

steps.title: רב: an egg is finished when it comes out
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא quotes רב: an egg becomes complete only when it is laid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רב: An egg is completed when it comes out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a statement from רב about eggs. The meaning is unclear, so the next steps will try to explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב says an egg is 'finished' at the moment it comes out of the hen. He does not say what practical law this affects. That gap is what the גמרא will now explore.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said in the name of Rav:
An egg is completed when it comes out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב: בֵּיצָה, עִם יְצִיאָתָהּ נִגְמְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new section with a fresh statement about eggs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An egg is considered complete only when it is laid.

steps.title: What does 'finished when it comes out' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of רב's statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'it is completed when it comes out' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what practical point רב was making. This sets up the suggested answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'finished when it comes out' could affect different laws. The גמרא will test possible meanings one at a time.

phrases.english: What does "it is completed when it comes out" mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״עִם יְצִיאָתָהּ נִגְמְרָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of רב's statement in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical law רב's statement is about

steps.title: First explanation, about milk, is challenged by a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב means an egg may be eaten with milk only after it is laid. It challenges this with a ברייתא that permits complete eggs found inside a slaughtered hen to be eaten with milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means that once it comes out it is finished and may be eaten with milk, that would mean that inside its mother it may not be eaten with milk. But a ברייתא teaches: If someone slaughters a hen and finds complete eggs inside, they may be eaten with milk!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one explanation of רב, about eating eggs with milk, and immediately attacks it with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב meant that an egg only stops counting as meat once it is laid, then a finished egg still inside the hen would count as meat and be forbidden with milk. The ברייתא says complete eggs found inside a slaughtered hen are permitted with milk. So this explanation of רב cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be tested)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is about eggs that are already complete inside the hen. Do not think it is talking about unfinished eggs.

phrases.english: If you say: when it comes out it is completed
and is permitted to be eaten with milk —

phrases.aramaic: הָא בִּמְעֵי אִמָּהּ אֲסוּרָה לְאׇכְלָה בְּחָלָב?
phrases.english: then inside its mother it is forbidden to eat with milk?
But it was taught in a ברייתא:
One who slaughters a hen
and finds complete eggs inside it —
they are permitted to be eaten with milk!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא, עִם יְצִיאָתָהּ נִגְמְרָה וּמוּתֶּרֶת לְאׇכְלָה בְּחָלָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to Step 10's question and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רב's statement is about eating eggs with milk
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The suggestion implies that complete eggs inside the hen are forbidden with milk, but a ברייתא explicitly permits them.

steps.title: Second explanation: the egg is permitted on יום טוב only once it is laid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב means an egg becomes permitted to eat on יום טוב only through being laid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב means: when the egg comes out, it is complete, and only then may it be eaten on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The milk explanation failed, so the גמרא offers a new meaning for רב's words. This one is about eating the egg on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic changes from milk and meat to the laws of יום טוב. According to this reading, an egg counts as a real egg for יום טוב purposes only after it has been laid, as long as it was laid before the holiday. This reading carries a hidden consequence that the next step will attack.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Signals that the previous explanation is dropped and a new one is offered.
With its coming out, meaning when it is laid.

phrases.english: Rather: with its emergence it becomes complete
and it is permitted to eat it on the Festival.
phrases.notes: This applies only if it was fully laid before יום טוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: עִם יְצִיאָתָהּ נִגְמְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected milk explanation from Step 11 with a יום טוב explanation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב was talking about eating eggs with milk.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב was talking about when an egg may be eaten on יום טוב.

steps.title: Challenge: a ברייתא permits eggs found inside a slaughtered hen
steps.stepSummary: If only laid eggs are permitted, eggs still inside the hen would be forbidden. But a ברייתא permits complete eggs found inside a slaughtered hen on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: That would mean an egg still inside its mother is forbidden to eat on יום טוב. But a ברייתא teaches that if someone slaughters a hen and finds complete eggs inside, he may eat them on יום טוב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws out what the new explanation implies and shows that a ברייתא says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being laid is what makes an egg permitted, then an unlaid egg would be forbidden. The ברייתא openly permits unlaid complete eggs taken from a slaughtered hen. This is the same ברייתא that was used in Step 11, now used against the יום טוב explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: This implies. Used to infer the opposite case.
But was it not taught in a ברייתא? Opens a challenge.

phrases.english: This implies that inside its mother
it is forbidden to eat it on the Festival?
But wasn't it taught:
One who slaughters the hen
and found fully formed eggs inside it
they are permitted to eat on the Festival!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא בִּמְעֵי אִמָּהּ אֲסוּרָה לְאׇכְלָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב? וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation proposed in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The יום טוב reading of רב's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reading implies unlaid eggs are forbidden on יום טוב, while the ברייתא explicitly permits them.

steps.title: Possible defense: the ברייתא teaches something the משנה did not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a way to save the explanation. The ruling about unlaid eggs comes only from a ברייתא and not from our משנה, so perhaps רב does not follow that ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: the ברייתא is teaching us something new that our משנה did not teach us, so רב can disagree with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible defense: perhaps רב simply holds differently from that ברייתא. The very next step will show that this does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא like רב has more room to differ from a ברייתא on a point that the משנה itself never addressed. The defense claims that our משנה says nothing about eggs inside the hen, so רב is free to forbid them. Whether this claim holds depends on whether the משנה really is silent about such eggs.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say. Introduces a possible defense that is often rejected right away.

phrases.english: And if you will say:
the ברייתא teaches us
what our משנה did not teach us,
phrases.notes: So רב, who follows the משנה, could disagree with the ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן בְּבָרַיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to defend Step 12 against the challenge in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the authority of the challenging source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא forces רב to permit unlaid eggs.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling is only in a ברייתא and not in the משנה, so רב may disagree with it.

steps.title: Rejected: our משנה itself implies that unlaid eggs are permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the defense. Our משנה shows that בית שמאי and בית הלל argue only about a laid egg, which implies that everyone permits eggs still inside the mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned this too in our משנה! 'An egg laid on יום טוב: בית שמאי say it may be eaten, and בית הלל say it may not be eaten.' They argue only about an egg that was laid. But eggs inside their mothers are permitted according to everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the משנה is not silent after all. It hints at the same ruling as the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes the argument as being about an egg 'laid on יום טוב'. That wording suggests that an egg still inside the hen is not part of the argument and is permitted by both sides. So the ברייתא teaches nothing new beyond the משנה, and רב could not disagree with it.

keyTerms.meaning: But we also learned this in the משנה.
They argue only up to this point, meaning their argument is limited to this case.

phrases.english: But this too we learned:
An egg that was laid on the Festival,
בית שמאי say: it may be eaten,
and בית הלל say: it may not be eaten.

phrases.aramaic: וְעַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: And בית שמאי and בית הלל only argue
about an egg that was laid,
but eggs inside their mothers
are permitted according to everyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense offered in Step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the משנה does not address eggs inside the hen.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's wording 'laid' implies that unlaid eggs are permitted by both schools.

steps.title: Possible defense: perhaps בית הלל forbid even eggs inside the hen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests reading the משנה differently. Perhaps בית הלל forbid even unlaid eggs, and the משנה said 'laid' only to show how far בית שמאי go in permitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that בית הלל forbid even eggs inside their mothers, and the משנה said 'laid' only to show the strength of בית שמאי's view, that they permit even an egg that was laid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second defense by reading the משנה another way. The next step will show the problem with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'laid' may have been chosen to show how far בית שמאי's leniency reaches: even a laid egg is permitted. If so, the משנה gives no proof about what בית הלל hold regarding unlaid eggs. Then רב could follow בית הלל and forbid them.

keyTerms.meaning: To show you their strength, meaning how far their opinion goes.

phrases.english: And if you will say that בית הלל
forbid even eggs inside their mothers,
and the reason it teaches 'laid'
is to show you the strength of בית שמאי
that they permit even a laid egg,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא בֵּית הִלֵּל אֲפִילּוּ בִּמְעֵי אִמָּן נָמֵי אָסְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to undo the inference from the משנה made in Step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'laid' implies that unlaid eggs are permitted by everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'laid' only highlights בית שמאי's leniency, and בית הלל may forbid unlaid eggs too.

steps.title: Rejected: the ברייתא would then match neither בית שמאי nor בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: If בית הלל forbid unlaid eggs, the ברייתא that permits them would follow neither school, and that cannot be.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then this ברייתא, 'one who slaughters a hen and finds complete eggs inside may eat them on יום טוב', whose view is it? It would be neither בית שמאי nor בית הלל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the second defense. The ברייתא would be left with no author.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי permit even laid eggs, but the ברייתא's wording suggests that only unlaid eggs are permitted, so it does not fit them. Under the defense, בית הלל forbid unlaid eggs, so it does not fit them either. Since a ברייתא cannot follow nobody, the defense fails, and with it the whole יום טוב explanation of רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Neither this one nor that one.

steps.confusionAlert: Why doesn't the ברייתא fit בית שמאי, if they are the lenient ones? By stressing eggs found inside the hen, the ברייתא implies that laid eggs would be forbidden. בית שמאי permit even laid eggs, so the ברייתא does not match their view.

phrases.english: But then that which was taught:
One who slaughters the hen
and found fully formed eggs inside it
they are permitted to eat on the Festival,
whose view is it?

phrases.aramaic: לָא בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וְלָא בֵּית הִלֵּל!
phrases.english: Neither בית שמאי nor בית הלל!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reinterpretation of the משנה offered in Step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that בית הלל forbid unlaid eggs, and with it the יום טוב explanation of רב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It leaves the ברייתא without any תנא who could have said it.

steps.title: Third explanation: only a laid egg can hatch chicks
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רב was not discussing any prohibition at all. He meant that only a laid egg is developed enough to hatch a chick, while an egg taken from inside the hen cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב means: when the egg comes out it is complete and can produce chicks. An egg still inside its mother cannot produce chicks.
steps.whatsHappening: Both איסור explanations have failed, so the גמרא gives a new meaning that has nothing to do with eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Complete' now refers to the natural readiness of the egg. A laid egg can be incubated and hatch, while an egg taken out of a slaughtered hen cannot. This removes every conflict with the ברייתא and the משנה, because רב is no longer forbidding anything.

keyTerms.meaning: Produces chicks, meaning it can hatch.

steps.whatToRemember: רב's statement 'an egg is complete only when laid' is not about milk or יום טוב. It means that only a laid egg can hatch a chick.

phrases.english: Rather: with its emergence it becomes complete
and it can produce chicks;
while inside its mother
it cannot produce chicks.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: עִם יְצִיאָתָהּ, נִגְמְרָה וּמְגַדֶּלֶת אֶפְרוֹחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected יום טוב explanation with a natural, physical meaning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation into a non-legal, factual statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב was ruling on whether eggs are permitted to eat.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב was describing which eggs are able to hatch.

steps.title: What practical difference does this make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why it matters in practice that only laid eggs can hatch.
steps.simpleTranslation: What practical difference does this make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב would bother to state a fact about nature. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A statement by an אמורא is expected to have some halachic effect. Since the new explanation is purely about nature, the גמרא asks where it makes a difference in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference comes out of it?

phrases.english: For what does it make a practical difference?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical relevance of the explanation in Step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical halachic difference of knowing that only laid eggs hatch.

steps.title: It matters for buying and selling
steps.stepSummary: The difference matters in business. A buyer of eggs for hatching must receive laid eggs, and the גמרא begins telling a story about this.
steps.simpleTranslation: For buying and selling. Like that man who said to people: 'Eggs...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the point matters in commerce. It then starts a story that continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone buys eggs in order to hatch chicks, eggs taken from a slaughtered hen are worthless for that purpose. Selling them for hatching could make the sale a mistaken deal. The story that begins here will show such a case.

keyTerms.meaning: Like that certain person. Introduces a story.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a natural fact can have real halachic effects in the laws of business dealings.

phrases.english: For buying and selling.
Like that man who said to them: 'Eggs'
phrases.notes: The story continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמִקָּח וּמִמְכָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference matters for commerce, where eggs that cannot hatch differ in value from eggs that can.
